## Integrating question

How are the elevation and dynamics of Peruvian tropical glaciers changing, and what roles may meteorology and light-absorbing particles play in that response?

<figure class="ma-figure-photo"><img src="/assets/img/photos/sections/agua-campo.webp" alt="High-mountain researchers next to glacial water during a field campaign" width="1400" height="933" loading="lazy"><div class="ma-photo-note"><span>MeteoAndes archive · 2026 campaigns</span><span>Site and authorship pending metadata validation</span></div><figcaption>The architecture combines field, laboratory and satellite observations; each sensor retains its own physical quantity and uncertainty.</figcaption></figure>

## Results matrix

| Component | Current result | Evidence level |
|---|---|---|
| ICESat‑2 Vilcanota | −1.463 m yr⁻¹; 95% CI: −2.357 to −0.596 | Consolidated/audited |
| InSAR Vilcanota | Suitable geometry; monthly signal near noise | Advanced diagnostic |
| Hydrometeorology | AOI/year panels; multi-year synthesis pending | Advanced diagnostic |
| Albedo/energy | Equations, QA/QC and forcing implemented | Implemented, not closed |
| AL30/AE33 | Preliminary eBC variability | Preliminary |
| SP2/ions | Preliminary profiles and multivariate analyses | Preliminary laboratory evidence |
| Sentinel‑5P | No validated final product | Pending |
